seo.title: AI Share of Voice: What It Is and How to Measure It
seo.meta_description: AI share of voice measures how often AI answers mention your brand versus competitors. How to choose prompts, score mentions, track it monthly and improve it.

h1: AI Share of Voice: How to Measure Your Brand's Presence in AI Answers
answer: AI share of voice is the percentage of relevant AI answers that mention your brand compared with competitors. To measure it, pick a fixed set of buyer questions, ask them in each major assistant on a regular schedule, record which brands are named and how, then divide your mentions by all brand mentions. Track it monthly to see the trend.
key_takeaways: AI share of voice compares your mentions with competitors' in AI answers.
Use a fixed set of real buyer questions.
Record position, sentiment and citations, not just mentions.
AI answers vary, so measure repeatedly and look at trends.
Improve it with clearer pages, consistency and third-party mentions.

sections.heading: What AI share of voice means
sections.body_html:
Share of voice is an old marketing idea: of all the attention in a market, how much goes to you? In AI search, the "attention" is the brands named in answers. If ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google's AI features answer twenty questions about your category and name brands forty times in total, and eight of those mentions are you, your AI share of voice is 20%.

It matters because AI answers are increasingly where buyers form a shortlist. A brand that is never named may never be considered.

sections.heading: Why it is different from rankings
sections.body_html: Traditional rank tracking checks one position for one keyword on one results page. AI answers are written fresh, can name several brands in one response, often vary from one run to the next, and differ between platforms. Pew Research Center found 88% of Google's AI summaries cited three or more sources, so the question is less "am I first?" and more "am I included, and how am I described?"

sections.heading: Step 1: choose the questions
sections.body_html:
1. Category questions: "best GEO agencies in Orange County", "top tools for X".
  2. Problem questions: "how do I get my business into ChatGPT answers".
  3. Comparison questions: "agency vs in-house for AI search".
  4. Brand questions: "is [your brand] good", "[your brand] reviews".

Twenty to fifty questions is a practical set for most businesses. Keep the wording fixed so results are comparable over time.

sections.heading: Step 2: choose platforms and settings
sections.body_html: Cover the assistants your buyers use: typically ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews or AI Mode, Gemini, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot and Claude. Note whether web search was on, the location the answer was given for, and the date. Logged-in personalization can affect results, so use consistent accounts or fresh sessions.

sections.heading: Step 3: record more than a yes or no
sections.body_html:
FieldWhat to record
MentionedWas your brand named?
PositionFirst, second or later in the answer
SentimentPositive, neutral or negative description
AccuracyWere the facts about you correct?
Cited sourceWhich page or site was linked
CompetitorsWhich other brands appeared

sections.heading: Step 4: calculate share of voice
sections.body_html: The basic formula is your mentions divided by all brand mentions across the question set, per platform and overall. A weighted version gives more credit to being named first or recommended positively. Whatever method you choose, keep it the same each month so the trend means something.

sections.heading: Account for variation
sections.body_html: The same question can produce different answers minutes apart. Run each question more than once per check, or across several days, and average the results. Look at month-over-month trends rather than reacting to a single answer. A change of a few percentage points may be noise; a steady climb over three months is a real signal.

sections.heading: Tools or spreadsheet?
sections.body_html: Dedicated AI visibility tools can automate prompts and scoring across platforms, which saves time at scale. A spreadsheet and a monthly routine work well for smaller question sets and cost nothing. Whichever you use, make sure you can see the actual answers, not just a score, because the wording tells you why you are or are not mentioned.

sections.heading: How to improve share of voice
sections.body_html:
• Fix access: make sure AI search crawlers can read your site.
  • Answer the questions directly on your own pages.
  • Be consistent: the same description of your business everywhere.
  • Earn third-party mentions: reviews, directories, roundups, press.
  • Correct inaccuracies at their source.

sections.heading: Connect it to business results
sections.body_html: Share of voice is a leading indicator. Pair it with AI referral traffic in analytics, branded search volume and leads by source. If share of voice rises and those follow, the program is working. If share of voice rises but leads do not, look at the questions you are tracking: they may not be the ones buyers ask before contacting a provider.

sections.heading: A simple monthly routine
sections.body_html: On the same day each month, run the question set on each platform, record the fields above, update the share-of-voice calculation, and note the three biggest changes and their likely causes. Share a one-page summary with the team. Over a quarter this builds a clear picture of where you are gaining and where competitors are pulling ahead.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: AI share of voice tells you how often buyers asking AI about your category hear your name instead of a competitor's. Measure it with a fixed set of real questions, the same platforms and the same method every month, and judge the trend, not a single answer.

faqs.q: What is AI share of voice?
faqs.a: The percentage of relevant AI answers, or brand mentions within them, that name your brand compared with competitors, measured across a fixed set of buyer questions.

faqs.q: How do I calculate AI share of voice?
faqs.a: Divide your brand mentions by all brand mentions across your question set, per platform and overall. Keep the method the same each month.

faqs.q: How many questions should I track?
faqs.a: Twenty to fifty real buyer questions is practical for most businesses, covering category, problem, comparison and brand questions.

faqs.q: Why do AI answers change between checks?
faqs.a: Answers are generated fresh and can vary by run, platform, location and settings. Repeat checks and focus on trends.

faqs.q: Which AI platforms should I track?
faqs.a: The ones your buyers use, typically ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews or AI Mode, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot and Claude.

faqs.q: Do I need a tool to measure AI share of voice?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. A spreadsheet and a monthly routine work for smaller question sets; tools help at scale.

faqs.q: How do I increase AI share of voice?
faqs.a: Make your site accessible to AI crawlers, answer buyer questions directly, keep brand details consistent and earn mentions on trusted sites.

faqs.q: Is AI share of voice the same as AI visibility?
faqs.a: It is one way to measure AI visibility. It focuses on how often you are named relative to competitors, alongside traffic and accuracy.
